occupants.value: An inferred household; no name is claimed
occupants.note: ADOPTED BY THE INFERRED-HOUSEHOLD PROGRAMME (docs/ROADMAP.md K1, phase two). This anonymous roof is the dwelling of an inferred blacksmith's household (2 of 3 this layer infers): hh_inf_blacksmith_north_02 in data/residents/households/. THE ROOF'S OWN EXISTENCE, POSITION AND FOOTPRINT REMAIN CONJECTURAL and are unchanged by the adoption; what the adoption adds is an argued occupant instead of an anonymous count-unit. The occupant is hypothesised from the town's demonstrable needs - the 1835 census of 3,265 people in 398 dwellings against the trades Andreas's 1833 roster names - and is not a person: no name is claimed and no figure is drawn.

residents.why: THE HOUSEHOLD IS HOUSED, WHICH IS THE POINT OF THE LAYER. recon_1835_north_d6_021 is an anonymous reconstructed roof already standing on the plat, adopted rather than duplicated: its existence, position and footprint stay conjectural and the adoption adds only the occupant argument. Which roof of the right family and district a hypothesised household occupies is not evidence about that roof; the household needed a dwelling and the programme assigned it one.
residents.basis: An anonymous roof of the reconstruction programme, ADOPTED by this household rather than raised for it. The roof's own existence and position stay conjectural; what the adoption adds is an argued occupant instead of an anonymous count-unit.

persons.name: Bryan Donnelly
persons.note: HYPOTHESISED, AND NOT A PERSON. No source names this resident and none is claimed to: the record asserts that a town of 3,265 people in 398 dwellings held at least this many households of this trade, and asserts nothing whatever about any individual. THE NAME IS INVENTED TOO, and `name_basis` beside it says so and says which pool it came from: this record used to carry a bare designation instead, on the reasoning that a surname would make it look like the documented layer, but a town of designations does not read as a town and the grade, this note and name_basis all say plainly which layer this is. No figure is drawn (docs/LIBERTIES.md L1). THE SECOND OF 3 BLACKSMITH HOUSEHOLDS THIS LAYER RECONSTRUCTS. THE OWNER'S OWN EXAMPLE, AND THE ARITHMETIC IS ALREADY IN THE DOCUMENTED LAYER. Five smiths are documented - Asahel Pierce, David McKee at the agency, Matthias Mason of 'Mason & Co.', Lemuel Brown, and the Rev. Mr See whose tools Pierce bought - and the reconstruction schedule allows six W1 blacksmith shops. This parcel builds Mason's documented third smithy and infers three more smith households, which brings the town to the schedule's six shops exactly: the smithies the wagon, plough and horse traffic of a town of 3,265 requires beyond the ones the sources happen to name.

residents.research_note: RECONSTRUCTED HOUSEHOLD - second of 3 blacksmith households in this layer, in the north division. THE OWNER'S OWN EXAMPLE, AND THE ARITHMETIC IS ALREADY IN THE DOCUMENTED LAYER. Five smiths are documented - Asahel Pierce, David McKee at the agency, Matthias Mason of 'Mason & Co.', Lemuel Brown, and the Rev. Mr See whose tools Pierce bought - and the reconstruction schedule allows six W1 blacksmith shops. This parcel builds Mason's documented third smithy and infers three more smith households, which brings the town to the schedule's six shops exactly: the smithies the wagon, plough and horse traffic of a town of 3,265 requires beyond the ones the sources happen to name. METHOD: the count comes from the occupation census in data/reconstruction/1835_inferred_household_programme.json, which calibrates every trade against three things this project already holds - the 1835 town census (3,265 people, 398 dwellings), Andreas's roster of the fall of 1833 (about fifty named people, most with a trade, in a settlement of some 350), and the reconstruction specification's roof schedule, whose workshop and store family targets are treated as the ceiling on a trade rather than as its measure. Every count is stated NET of the documented layer: this dataset infers a tradesman only where it cannot name one.
